prerequisites: Students must have previously passed the subjects 'Technical Thermodynamics and Fundamentals of Heat Transfer' and 'Thermal Engineering'.
Knowledge of the fundamental concepts of fluid mechanics and machine design is recommended.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of applied thermodynamics and heat transfer. Basic principles and their application to solving engineering problems.
Applied knowledge of the fundamentals of fluid-mechanical systems and machines.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, work plans and other similar tasks.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knows the different typologies of thermoelectric power plants and thermal turbomachinery.
Knows and understands the operation of thermoelectric power plants and thermal turbomachinery.
Applies techniques and methods from various disciplines for the analysis and design of thermoelectric power plants and thermal turbomachinery.
Knows and understands the control and regulation systems of thermoelectric power plants and thermal turbomachinery.
Knows the fundamentals of the economic and environmental analyses of thermoelectric power plants.
Knows the operation and maintenance of thermoelectric power plants and thermal turbomachinery.

syllabus_topics: Control and regulation of thermoelectric power plants
Energy and exergy analysis of thermoelectric power plants
Environmental analysis of thermoelectric power plants
teaching_methods: Laboratory practices and/or with computer tools
Formulation of additional exercises, questions, and problems
assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated by weighting the grades of each part. If tutored works are completed, the written exam accounts for 70%, tutored works 20%, and practical activities 10%. If tutored works are not completed, the written exam accounts for 90% and practical activities 10%. Students who do not pass practical activities during the semester or wish to improve their grade can take a practical exam, which will account for 10% of the final grade. Students must be able to prove authorship of all submitted work.
